tagline: A winding lakeshore road links eagle country with a rebuilt lumber town.
intro: Idaho 97 winds along the east side of Lake Coeur d’Alene on two paved lanes with few places to pass. The entire highway is designated the Lake Coeur d’Alene Scenic Byway. Visit Idaho presents the drive as a route through rugged mountains, with wildlife and panoramic views. Along the shore, the road follows the foot of hills belonging to the Coeur d’Alene National Forest.

This eastern lakeshore route was formerly part of U.S. Route 95 Alternate, a designation that lasted until 1977. At Harrison, another transportation story survives in the Trail of the Coeur d’Alenes, which uses the former Union Pacific Railroad right-of-way. The trail runs from Plummer to Mullan. Harrison’s earlier economy depended on water as well as rails: the lake and its two major rivers carried timber out of the forests, and millions of board feet were stored in the lake at town.

Starting at Interstate 90 at Wolf Lodge Bay, the southbound drive reaches Beauty Bay and the Mineral Ridge Trail, then continues through gentle hills and dense forests toward Harrison. The Coeur d’Alene River crossing comes before Harrison; beyond town, Idaho 97 heads southeast through the Coeur d’Alene Reservation to Idaho 3. There the byway meets the White Pine Scenic Byway.
notice: South of Beauty Bay, the route continues through gentle hills and dense forests toward Harrison.

moments.title: Wolf Lodge Bay
moments.text: Bald eagles feed on kokanee in Lake Coeur d’Alene, with Wolf Lodge Bay a place to watch that seasonal gathering. December and January are the peak eagle-watching months along the shore between Wolf Lodge Bay and Beauty Bay. The fish have their own history in these waters: kokanee were stocked by the Idaho Department of Fish and Game. Kokanee were introduced to improve fishing; native fish in the lake included bull trout, westslope cutthroat and whitefish. This bay also marks the highway’s northern end, where Idaho 97 meets Interstate 90.

moments.title: Mineral Ridge Trail
moments.text: At Beauty Bay, Mineral Ridge offers a view across the lake and a closer look at the forest. Ponderosa pine and Douglas fir are the trail’s two main tree types. Construction began in 1963; National Recreation Trail designation followed in 1982. The 3.3-mile route has a self-guided interpretive tour, with learning stations explaining local plants and animal life. The Bureau of Land Management administers this backcountry hiking area near Lake Coeur d’Alene. Along the eastern shoreline of Lake Coeur d’Alene, the byway also passes habitat for bald eagles and nesting osprey.

moments.title: Harrison
moments.text: Brick buildings and a city park mark different responses to Harrison’s 1917 fire. The blaze began at the Grant Lumber Company and consumed about half the residential area and about half the business district. Much of the town was never rebuilt. Some business owners rebuilt in fireproof construction, leaving the commercial historic district with six brick buildings from 1917 or shortly afterward. A city block that was not rebuilt became a park. The district follows Coeur d’Alene Avenue, also Idaho 97, with the park among the buildings on its west side.
